title: Taking the Meeting Outside
transcript: Our office tried walking meetings after staff said short catch-ups often got postponed because the meeting rooms were booked. Pairs chose a loop around the block and noted what they had achieved when they returned. The walks worked well for sorting out priorities or talking through an idea. People struggled when they had to check figures, because stopping to read a spreadsheet on a phone interrupted the conversation. One pair also found that traffic drowned out parts of their discussion near the main road. By the end of the trial, the team had marked a quieter loop and reserved walking meetings for topics people could discuss without consulting documents.

questions.prompt: What prompted the office to try walking meetings?
options: Short conversations were delayed by a shortage of available rooms.
Staff wanted more opportunities to meet colleagues from other teams.
Managers needed to reduce the length of weekly presentations.
Employees were having trouble joining calls from their desks.
questions.answer: Short conversations were delayed by a shortage of available rooms.
questions.explanation: 会议室经常被订满，导致简短的工作交流一再推迟。

questions.prompt: Which meeting would most likely stay indoors under the final arrangement?
options: A brief discussion about who should greet a visitor.
A review requiring colleagues to check figures against a spreadsheet.
A conversation about possible names for a project.
A catch-up to agree on the order of next week's tasks.
questions.answer: A review requiring colleagues to check figures against a spreadsheet.
questions.explanation: 试行后，团队只把无需查阅文件的话题安排到户外，因此需要核对表格数据的会议更适合留在室内。

section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
